filmhouse.title: A Poet
filmhouse.description: Oscar is an aging, rueful poet whose artistic ambitions have long faded into obscurity and heavy drinking. When Oscar takes up teaching to meet ends meet, he encounters Yurlady, a working-class girl with an extraordinary gift for poetry, he becomes consumed with launching her talent into the local literary scene. Driven by a desperate longing for career redemption and a second chance at fatherhood, Oscar inadvertently pushes her into an ambitious world she never asked to join. Directed by Simón Mesa Soto, this tragicomedy earned the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and represented Colombia as its official submission for Best International Feature Film. Anchored by a brilliant, cringe-inducing performance from Ubeimar Rios, the film offers a darkly funny and deeply humane satire on artist egos and the messy search for purpose. A Poet, A Creative, A Panel Join us for a post-show fireside chat on Tue 6 Oct, 7.30pm ! Do you dream of writing your story one day? Of writing novels, poetry, or making films? Do you want to support those dreamers around us to do so? It isn’t easy being an artist anywhere, especially not outside major commercial systems like America, the UK, and Hollywood. And though A POET comes from halfway across the world, our creative industries are really not so different. So why make the admirably Herculean task of creating any harder by keeping career wisdom behind closed doors (or gates), or by having to struggle alone? And if you care about local voices, then how can we best support our artists? Join us for a fireside chat with a local poet, Theophilus Kwek , and filmmaker, Pek Jia Hao , as they share with us their uncensored stories, tips and tricks, and dreams for the creative life in Singapore. In Spanish with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Nudity.

filmhouse.title: The Invite
filmhouse.description: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
filmhouse.description: Haru, a competitive ballroom dancer in Tokyo, finds her world shattered when a sudden tragedy takes her husband-cum-dance partner from her side. Withdrawn into deep isolation and grief, she slowly allows her friends to coax her back onto the floor, where an unexpected connection with a new instructor reignites her passion. As she navigates life after loss, Haru stumbles through awkward choices, finding that healing is an exuberant, messy, and wildly colorful process. Featuring a charismatic lead performance by Rinko Kikuchi(Pacific Rim), the film presents an energetic, unabashed and fantastical way of moving on. In Japanese, Spanish and English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scene and Mature Content.

filmhouse.title: Cyber City Oedo 808
filmhouse.description: In a dystopian 29th-century Tokyo, three hardened criminals, Sengoku, Gogul, and Benten are released from an orbital prison to serve as a high tech penal police force. Outfitted with explosive collars that detonate if they disobey, the trio is dispatched to hunt down lethal cyber terrorists, rogue Androids, and mutated corporate experiments in exchange for reductions in their century long sentences. A foundational pillar of 1990s anime cyberpunk, Kawajiri’s signature neon noir aesthetic, fluid kinetic violence, and intricate mechanical designs by Takashi Watabe (Akira) directly influenced Western sci-fi landmarks like The Matrix. In its 2K restoration, the film’s striking hand drawn cel animation, rich shadow work, and vivid cyberpunk palette pop with high definition clarity *The original 3-Part OVA will be shown in one continuous sitting. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Violence and Some Nudity. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audience are advised.

filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: No Country for Old Men
filmhouse.description: Llewelyn Moss stumbles upon dead bodies, $2 million and a hoard of heroin in a Texas desert, but methodical killer Anton Chigurh comes looking for it, with local sheriff Ed Tom Bell hot on his trail. The roles of prey and predator blur as the violent pursuit of money and justice collide. In English. Rated NC16 for Violence.

filmhouse.title: Aftersun
filmhouse.description: On a quiet summer holiday at a Turkish resort in the late 1990s, 11-year-old Sophie spends precious days with her loving, idealistic father, Calum. Decades later, an adult Sophie revisits home video footage and fragmented memories from the trip, attempting to reconcile the father she remembered with the personal struggles he kept hidden from view. Charlotte Wells’ remarkable debut feature earned Paul Mescal an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor alongside the French Touch Prize at the Cannes Film Festival. A deeply felt portrait of memory, grief, and parental love, the film pairs subtle visual storytelling with remarkable central performances that linger long after the credits roll. In English. Rated M18 for Mature Content. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audiences are advised.

filmhouse.title: Amrum
filmhouse.description: Spring 1945, the remote North Sea island of Amrum. In what will become the final days of World War II, big-hearted young student Nanning (exceptional newcomer Jasper Billerbeck) has a busy life. He braves the treacherous sea to hunt seals, fishes at night, and works the neighbouring potato farm run by Tessa (Diane Kruger) to help his pregnant mother Hille (Laura Tonke) – a fervent Nazi loyalist - feed the family. His father, captured as a prisoner of war, is unable to offer help or guidance to his son. When a radio broadcast brings news of Hitler’s fall, Nanning’s world begins to unravel. His devastated mother refuses to eat anything other than white bread, butter and honey. Craving her affection, the ever-enterprising Nanning embarks on a quest across the island to obtain these precious, near-impossible to find ingredients... In German with English subtitles. Rating PG. Some Disturbing Scenes Presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore in collaboration with Filmhouse TW: Contains depictions of animal cruelty.

filmhouse.title: Digger
filmhouse.description: Digger Rockwell (Tom Cruise) is a megalomaniacal oil tycoon and one of the most powerful men on the planet. When his reckless deep-sea drilling operation in Greenland triggers a catastrophic environmental disaster, Digger refuses to back down or accept blame. Instead, he launches a frantic, delusional public relations crusade to spin the catastrophe, attempting to convince an unraveling world that he is humanity’s ultimate savior before the consequences of his hubris destroy everything. Four-time Academy Award winner Alejandro González Iñárritu ( Birdman , The Revenant ) returns to English language filmmaking with a blistering, absurdist black comedy. Anchored by Cruise’s most unhinged, transformative lead performance in decades, the film features a stellar supporting ensemble including Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons. Shot entirely on 35mm VistaVision by master cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, Digger pairs razor sharp political satire with sweeping visual scale, an audacious, large-format spectacle engineered specifically for the big screen experience. In English with English & Chinese subtitles Rated M18 for Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: The Big Lebowski
filmhouse.description: Jeffrey 'The Dude' Lebowski, a Los Angeles slacker who only wants to bowl and drink White Russians, is mistaken for another Jeffrey Lebowski, a wheelchair-bound millionaire, and finds himself dragged into a strange series of events involving nihilists, adult film producers, ferrets, errant toes, and large sums of money. In English. Rated M18 for Coarse Language Come dressed as your favourite Lebowski character and get 10% off at the bar

filmhouse.title: Stalker
filmhouse.description: A faithful stalker guides a melancholic writer and a skeptical scientist into the Zone, a stretch of heavily guarded land where the ordinary laws of physics no longer apply. At its centre lies a room said to grant a person's deepest, innermost desires. Tarkovsky's most well known masterpiece, Stalker, turns the spectacle of the Zone into an introspection for the three men inside it. In this liminal nothingness, the camera lingers on moss and rust and water until stillness feels comfortable. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness ’ In Russian with English subtitles. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: Before Sunset
filmhouse.description: Nine years after their chance encounter in Vienna, American author Jesse and French environmentalist Céline cross paths once more in a Paris bookstore on the final leg of Jesse’s European book tour. With barely an hour before Jesse must catch his flight back to the United States, the pair wander through sunlit Parisian alleyways, quiet cafes, and a barge along the Seine. As their casual catch-up unfolds in near real-time, playful conversation rapidly gives way to an intimate confrontation with lost time, unfulfilled promises, and the quiet regrets of adulthood. Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, Richard Linklater’s second entry in his seminal Before trilogy is a masterpiece of naturalistic, dialogue-driven cinema. Co-written by Linklater, Ethan Hawke, and Julie Delpy, the film builds extraordinary emotional tension through razor-sharp honesty, precise pacing, and effortless chemistry between its leads. In English. Rated NC16.

filmhouse.title: Moonlight (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Framed across three pivotal eras of his life, Chiron navigates the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood while struggling with his identity, sexuality, and a troubled home environment. Guided by the tender mentorship of a local drug dealer and a deep, enduring connection with a childhood friend, Chiron gradually leanrs to protect himself from the world as he grows into adulthood. Directed by Barry Jenkins, this groundbreaking drama won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Mahershala Ali. Celebrated for James Laxton’s luminous cinematography and Nicholas Britell’s evocative score, the film stands as a transcendent, deeply lyrical portrait of intimacy, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Newly restored in 4K and with an exclusive conversation with director Barry Jenkins, featuring Oscar Nominated composer Nicholas Britell and Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, to follow the feature. In English. Rated M18 for Some Homosexual Content.

filmhouse.title: Extrawurst
filmhouse.description: At a routine general meeting of a tranquil, provincial tennis club, Heribert (Hape Kerkeling), long-time chairman of the club, and his ambitious deputy Matthias (Friedrich Mücke, Balloon) put forward a simple vote on the purchase of a barbeque grill for the next club party. However, Melanie (Anja Knauer) unexpectedly ignites a cultural clash when she suggests buying a second grill for her doubles partner Erol (Fahri Yardim), the club’s only Turkish member, because devout Muslims cannot eat food cooked alongside pork. What starts as a thoughtful gesture quickly snowballs into a heated debate about much more than a grill but instead, roasting each other. As atheists are pitted against believers, progressives against traditionalists, soon the discussion escalates until the club is brought to the brink of collapse. In German with English subtitles. Rating NC16. Some Mature Content Presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore in collaboration with Filmhouse

filmhouse.title: Stop Making Sense (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Some movies are meant to be watched in quiet contemplation; others demand to be experienced as a party. We are cranking up Filmhouse’s 7.1 sound system to present the definitive 4K restoration of Talking Heads’ cinematic milestone in all its high volume glory! Captured over three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theatre in 1983, Jonathan Demme’s concert film opens on an empty stage with David Byrne, an acoustic guitar, and a portable cassette player performing "Psycho Killer." Musician by musician, instrument by instrument, the stage is constructed before the audience's eyes, escalating into an exhilarating, high energy spectacle driven by Talking Heads at the peak of their live performance powers. Whether you're a lifelong fan or discovering the iconic big suit for the first time, join us for an unmissable communal screening that bridges the gap between cinema and live concert! In English. Rated PG TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audiences are advised.

filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: Exile
filmhouse.description: A Kosovan of migrant background living in Germany believes he's a victim of xenophobia, but it may be his own paranoia spiraling out of control. The psychological drama-thriller Exile, directed by Visar Morina, stands as a poignant exploration of integration, identity, and the insidious nature of psychological alienation within a modern European context. Starring Mišel Matičević as Xhafer and Sandra Hüller as Nora, the film subverts the traditional narrative of the struggling immigrant by focusing on an affluent, professional protagonist who has seemingly achieved the pinnacle of assimilation. Through its claustrophobic storytelling, Exile blurs the lines between objective workplace discrimination and subjective paranoia, mapping out a devastating portrait of a man whose sense of belonging systematically unravels. In Albanian, French and German with English subtitles. Rating M18. Nudity Presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore in collaboration with Filmhouse

filmhouse.title: Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust
filmhouse.description: Set in a future gothic wasteland where ancient vampires dominate a fading world, "D" a half vampire, half human bounty hunter is hired to retrieve a wealthy family's daughter abducted by a powerful vampire nobleman. Racing against the ruthless Markus Brothers, a rival band of mercenary hunters, D encounters a complex web of forbidden romance, tragic monstrousness, and dark fantasy. Widely regarded as Kawajiri’s directorial masterpiece, Bloodlust showcases the artistry of pre digital, hand drawn Japanese animation with its blend of Baroque grandeur, dark romanticism, and dazzling action choreography. The 2K restoration elevates Yoshitaka Amano's breathtaking character designs and painterly background art, restoring the film's velvet shadow tones and fine line work to pristine quality In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Violence and Nudity. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.

filmhouse.title: Fargo (30th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Jerry, a small-town Minnesota car salesman is bursting at the seams with debt... but he's got a plan. He's going to hire two thugs to kidnap his wife in a scheme to collect a hefty ransom from his wealthy father-in-law. It's going to be a snap and nobody's going to get hurt... until people start dying. Enter Police Chief Marge, a coffee-drinking, parka-wearing - and extremely pregnant - investigator who'll stop at nothing to get her man. And if you think her small-time investigative skills will give the crooks a run for their ransom... you betcha! In English Rated M18 for Violence.

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Moonlight (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Framed across three pivotal eras of his life, Chiron navigates the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood while struggling with his identity, sexuality, and a troubled home environment. Guided by the tender mentorship of a local drug dealer and a deep, enduring connection with a childhood friend, Chiron gradually leanrs to protect himself from the world as he grows into adulthood. Directed by Barry Jenkins, this groundbreaking drama won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Mahershala Ali. Celebrated for James Laxton’s luminous cinematography and Nicholas Britell’s evocative score, the film stands as a transcendent, deeply lyrical portrait of intimacy, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Newly restored in 4K and with an exclusive conversation with director Barry Jenkins, featuring Oscar Nominated composer Nicholas Britell and Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, to follow the feature. In English. Rated M18 for Some Homosexual Content.

filmhouse.title: Digger
filmhouse.description: Digger Rockwell (Tom Cruise) is a megalomaniacal oil tycoon and one of the most powerful men on the planet. When his reckless deep-sea drilling operation in Greenland triggers a catastrophic environmental disaster, Digger refuses to back down or accept blame. Instead, he launches a frantic, delusional public relations crusade to spin the catastrophe, attempting to convince an unraveling world that he is humanity’s ultimate savior before the consequences of his hubris destroy everything. Four-time Academy Award winner Alejandro González Iñárritu ( Birdman , The Revenant ) returns to English language filmmaking with a blistering, absurdist black comedy. Anchored by Cruise’s most unhinged, transformative lead performance in decades, the film features a stellar supporting ensemble including Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons. Shot entirely on 35mm VistaVision by master cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, Digger pairs razor sharp political satire with sweeping visual scale, an audacious, large-format spectacle engineered specifically for the big screen experience. In English with English & Chinese subtitles Rated M18 for Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
filmhouse.description: Haru, a competitive ballroom dancer in Tokyo, finds her world shattered when a sudden tragedy takes her husband-cum-dance partner from her side. Withdrawn into deep isolation and grief, she slowly allows her friends to coax her back onto the floor, where an unexpected connection with a new instructor reignites her passion. As she navigates life after loss, Haru stumbles through awkward choices, finding that healing is an exuberant, messy, and wildly colorful process. Featuring a charismatic lead performance by Rinko Kikuchi(Pacific Rim), the film presents an energetic, unabashed and fantastical way of moving on. In Japanese, Spanish and English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scene and Mature Content.

filmhouse.title: The Invite
filmhouse.description: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: We Are All Strangers
filmhouse.description: A life-altering event forces 21-year-old Junyang and his girlfriend to face reality. At the same time, while Junyang’s father is struggling to hold their modest life together, a woman enters his life and both generations are forced to redefine their family. Cast Q&A, Sun 6 Sep Join us for an in-person Q&A with Cast Members, Andi Lim, Koh Jia Ler and Regene Lim, moderated by Petrina Kow. In Mandarin and English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language and Sexual References. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.

filmhouse.title: Trainspotting (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Danny Boyle's decade-defining adaptation of Irvine Welsh's Trainspotting celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2026, and is heading back to Filmhouse from 21 August in a 4K restoration as part of our Music In Film showcase! Ewan McGregor stars as Mark Renton, the most reflective member of a group that also includes the compulsive womaniser, Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), and the hapless Spud (Ewen Bremner). Renton, Spud and Sick Boy's issues with drugs alternatively irritate and amuse their friend, Begbie (Robert Carlyle), a periodic psychopath whose outbursts of violence are one of the many factors that convince Renton to leave for London in the hope of starting a new life. Renton enjoys some success remoulding himself as an estate agent in the English capital, but it isn't long before his Edinburgh friends catch up with him. Begbie and co. need the money Renton has saved from his job to finance the drug deal that could make them all rich... In English with English subtitles. Rated R21 for Drug Use and Sexual Scenes

filmhouse.title: Tony
filmhouse.description: Discover how the iconic Anthony Bourdain came to be in Matt Johnson’s scrappy coming-of-age comedy that's equal parts sweet and sour. Long before he became the world’s favorite culinary storyteller, Anthony Bourdain was just a dishwashing kid getting baptized in the grease, sweat, and chaos of a 1970s coastal seafood shack. This electric origin story follows a young Tony (Dominic Sessa) as he gets thrown into the fire of a cutthroat kitchen brigade. Surrounded by foul-mouthed line cooks, late-night vices, and non-stop pressure, a reckless teenager stumbles into the raw grit and rock-and-roll pulse that defined his entire legacy. In English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Coarse Language and Drug Use. The film contains an utterance of religious profanity that exceeds IMDA guidelines. The line has been muted by the distributor to be kept in line with guidelines.

filmhouse.title: A Poet
filmhouse.description: Oscar is an aging, rueful poet whose artistic ambitions have long faded into obscurity and heavy drinking. When Oscar takes up teaching to meet ends meet, he encounters Yurlady, a working-class girl with an extraordinary gift for poetry, he becomes consumed with launching her talent into the local literary scene. Driven by a desperate longing for career redemption and a second chance at fatherhood, Oscar inadvertently pushes her into an ambitious world she never asked to join. Directed by Simón Mesa Soto, this tragicomedy earned the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and represented Colombia as its official submission for Best International Feature Film. Anchored by a brilliant, cringe-inducing performance from Ubeimar Rios, the film offers a darkly funny and deeply humane satire on artist egos and the messy search for purpose. A Poet, A Creative, A Panel Join us for a post-show fireside chat on Tue 6 Oct, 7.30pm ! Do you dream of writing your story one day? Of writing novels, poetry, or making films? Do you want to support those dreamers around us to do so? It isn’t easy being an artist anywhere, especially not outside major commercial systems like America, the UK, and Hollywood. And though A POET comes from halfway across the world, our creative industries are really not so different. So why make the admirably Herculean task of creating any harder by keeping career wisdom behind closed doors (or gates), or by having to struggle alone? And if you care about local voices, then how can we best support our artists? Join us for a fireside chat with a local poet, Theophilus Kwek , and filmmaker, Pek Jia Hao , as they share with us their uncensored stories, tips and tricks, and dreams for the creative life in Singapore. In Spanish with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Nudity.

She repeatedly appears at crime scenes where police have ruled as suicides or accidents. Officer Wong Ming (Carlos Chan) initially believes that she is mentally unstable, until he discovers that she has the ability to communicate with the dead. As the two investigate the victims, they uncover a sinister conspiracy. With the true mastermind lurking in the shadows, Lan Pui-ching must overcome the inner demons that have haunted her for 13 years and stop the next murder in a world where science and supernatural collide.

upcoming.description: Following the death of his father (Josh Brolin), Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) goes diving off the central Coast of California in search of his remains, but is swallowed by a massive sperm whale. While trapped inside its belly with only one hour of oxygen left, Jay comes to realize that the hard-earned lessons his father imparted may be the key to his escape.

upcoming.title: Clayface
upcoming.description: DC Studios’ first-ever foray into the genre, “Clayface” is a horror thriller from director James Watkins, starring Tom Rhys Harries in the title role of the Gotham City villain. It unravels one man’s horrifying descent from rising Hollywood star to revenge-filled monster in a story that explores the loss of one’s identity and humanity, corrosive love, and the dark underbelly of scientific ambition.

upcoming.title: Henry's First Dates (THAI)
upcoming.description:
They say the first date is the most exciting moment in any relationship —
a feeling you only get once! Except for ‘Lucy’ (Minnie Nicha Yontararak), who’s
living her first date on repeat with ‘Henry’ (Nadech Kugimiya), a good-natured,
animal-loving guy with a bizarre condition: every time he wakes up, he can’t
remember anything from the day before. So, Lucy has to find a way to keep
wooing Henry, to make him fall in love with her every singe day. And that’s before
she even gets past his family and the people closest to him: Dad (Kiat Kitjaroen),
Ka-noon (Ble Patoomrach), and Auntie Su (Tipagorn Chaiprasit). Can Lucy make
Henry fall for her, again and again? Or will he forget her… forever?

upcoming.title: The Weight

It stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi.

upcoming.description: In the wonderfully whimsical tradition of Dr. Seuss, The Cat in the Hat comes to the big screen in his animated theatrical feature film debut, doing what he does best— spreading joy to “happyless” kids. In the film, The Cat takes on his toughest assignment yet… to cheer a pair of siblings struggling with their move to a new town.

upcoming.description: Twins Alfie and Elise find a magical Wish Watch on Christmas Eve and are swept by the Wish Collector into the musical Land of Sometimes, where they learn that wishes have consequences.

upcoming.description: This November, Johnny Depp is Ebenezer Scrooge. The name you know, the story you don’t. EBENEZER follows a miserly businessman who is forced through visions of the past, present, and future during a supernatural journey toward a chance at redemption.

upcoming.description: Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson are part of a group of bank robbers who share their heists on social media in this tongue-in-cheek thriller from the director of Bullet Train.

upcoming.description: In present-day Paris, dancer Anastasia joins the Opéra Garnier. While rehearsing the cursed opera Orpheus, supposedly written by the Phantom, she falls for a mysterious pianist. As opening night approaches, strange accidents occur.

upcoming.title: Disney's Hexed
upcoming.description: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

upcoming.description: The circle of trust just got bigger. This November, comedy icon and Emmy winner Ben Stiller and two-time Oscar winner Robert De Niro reunite, joined by Grammy winner and Oscar nominee Ariana Grande, in Focker-In-Law, a new chapter in the blockbuster Meet the Parents franchise.

upcoming.title: Asterix: The Kingdom of Nubia
upcoming.description: The irreductible Gauls are turned into harmless children after a rare youth elixir accidentally ends up into the magic potion. To find the antidote, Asterix and Obelix embark on a crazy journey to the far away Kingdom of Nubia.

Sapped of his magic, he'll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell).
